structured.approach:
I followed the design-steps skill for DES-03, where the workbook defines no action. I treated the step as a developer-readiness review.
- I read the three contracted inputs: feat.design, feat.stories and feat.trd. I also read the approved feat.screens as background through context_get.
- Read as each coding lane would before starting, I listed every doubt about behaviour, edge cases, tests and CI. I answered each one from an approved source. Where no source answered, I stated an interim assumption and gave it an owner.
- To ground the CI and process answers, I read each repository's ci.py / ci.mjs and CLAUDE.md, ap_portal's package.json, the DES-02 gate decisions and the feature's COMMUNICATION.md. Shell commands were denied for this step (G9), so nothing was executed. Statements about Python behaviour are marked as agent judgement.
- I compared the three inputs with each other. Six differences were found, all in form only. I set a precedence rule: stories and TRD define what must hold, the approved design defines how.
- I ran the verifier subagent on the draft. It found 8 problems: over-broad statements, one wrong section reference and some uncited process claims. I fixed all 8.
- No connector was needed.

claims.text: The DES-02 approvals by the Architect and the UX lead carry only the comment 'automated checks and the independent judge passed' and record no answer to the TRD questions, so the lanes build on the design's interim answers and the stories' [Pending] markers stay.
The design maps interim answers to TRD questions: TQ-3 to DD-3, TQ-6 to the allow-list, TQ-7 to the plain header row, TQ-9 to KeyError, TQ-10 to DD-6 and TQ-11 to DD-5.

The TRD types the delays_by_vendor input as List[Dict] and tests paid with record["paid"], while the design uses Iterable[Dict] and record.get("paid"); the clarifications follow the design because the behaviour for pipeline records is the same.
The paid_date check must run after the existing try block and append the literal reason 'paid_date'; otherwise the reason would be the exception type name.
bucket_for returns '31-60' for exactly 30 days, so overdue_with_risk must apply days > 30 itself and must not call bucket_for.
The existing forecast test expects predict_delay_days([-5, 5]) to return 2, so the boundary tests for vendor_risk should use histories whose rounded prediction is exact.

Python CI compiles with whatever interpreter runs /usr/bin/python3 ci.py and has no Python 3.9 syntax gate. It flags print, eval, exec, bare except and lines over 140 characters, and requires coverage of at least 90.
ap_portal CI runs tests/*.test.js with NODE_PATH=src and flags any line matching console.log or eval( (comments included), lines over 140 characters, and line coverage below 90.
The ap_portal version 2.3.0 appears in both src/ap_portal/index.js and package.json, although the repository note names only index.js; both should be stepped together.
Branches follow main, dev and feature/<story>, and commit messages start with the story ID.
The exact expected portal output is the one-line table in feat.screens FS-1, with no thead/tbody and no tokens, and the empty state renders an empty string.
The design's ap_portal test list covers only the non-string-amount TypeError branch; tests for non-array rows and non-integer days are added as clarifications to keep coverage at the CI threshold.
The feature issue accepts answers in the form '/answer <STEP>: <text>', which this file proposes as the loop for new developer doubts.

open_questions: CQ-1 (non-blocking, Architect/PM): Should ap_pipeline to_model reject non-finite amounts such as NaN or Infinity? Interim: out of scope, no handling added.
CQ-2 (non-blocking, Architect): Should renderOverdueRisk throw TypeError for a non-string id or vendor, like the amount and days checks? Interim: String(value), no check.
CQ-3 (non-blocking, Architect/DevOps): Which Python version is /usr/bin/python3 on the CI host, and should CI add a Python 3.9 syntax gate? Interim: developers keep to 3.9 syntax themselves.
CQ-4 (non-blocking, Architect; part of TQ-4): Should build_explanation_request restrict risk to high/medium/low? Interim: any non-None value is appended.
CQ-5 (non-blocking, PM/DES-04): Should branches and commits use the feat.stories labels or the task IDs DES-04 creates? Interim: the story labels.
CQ-6 (non-blocking, Architect): Should overdue_with_risk reject a float amount with TypeError? Interim: no guard.
Carried, still open and non-blocking: TQ-1 to TQ-11, DQ-1 to DQ-5, SQ-1 to SQ-4, OQ-B1 to OQ-B10, PQ-1 to PQ-6 and PQ-P1 to PQ-P7.
